title: Texas franchise tax: who is taxable, when reports are due, and the no-tax-due threshold
rule: Texas franchise tax applies to taxable entities formed in Texas or doing business there, including LLCs and limited partnerships; a general partnership owned directly and entirely by natural persons, without limited liability, is not taxable. Reports are due May 15, starting the year after the entity becomes subject to the tax. For reports due in 2026 and 2027, an entity with revenue at or below $2.65 million owes no tax and files only a Public Information or Ownership Information Report.
changeWatch: The no-tax-due threshold is adjusted on January 1 of each even-numbered year (next in 2028); also watch amendments to Tax Code chapter 171 and Comptroller Rule 3.584.
